sections.h2: Who records deeds in Sanilac County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Any paper that changes or burdens title to land in this county is filed with the recorder in Sandusky. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, easements, liens, plats, surveys and court orders about real estate all get indexed there, using one uniform system and fees fixed by state law.

Drafting is outside its job: staff will not write a deed or give legal advice, so have an attorney or title agent prepare yours. Once a document exists, the office answers practical questions at (810) 648-2313, and the county's department page links to forms, fee schedules and requirements.

A weekly land transfer list is posted on the same site, naming the parties and the section and township for each deed that cleared that week. The county spans 963 square miles of land, the most of any Lower Peninsula county, so those sections range from farm acreage in the Thumb to cottages near the Lake Huron shore.

sections.h2: What will recording a Sanilac County deed cost?
sections.html:
Expect $30 to put a deed on record, plus $8.60 in transfer taxes per $1,000 of price. The table gathers the amounts a seller meets most often.

What the Sanilac County fee schedule charges around a sale
ItemAmountAuthority
Base charge to record a deed or mortgage$30 whatever the lengthMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Surcharge per additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3MCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5County fee schedule
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000MCL 207.504
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000MCL 207.525
Paper copies from the land records$1 a page, $5 to certifyCounty fee schedule

Try a $160,000 house: 160 thousands at $8.60 is $1,376 in transfer tax, and the recording fee and treasurer's certificate bring the government total to $1,411.

sections.h2: Who owes the transfer tax on a Sanilac County sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. State law puts the tax on the grantor and gives 15 days after delivery of the deed to pay the county treasurer, though at the Sanilac counter it is collected as the deed is recorded.

Put the full value of the land on the face of the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. A sale that bundles a house with furniture or equipment is taxed on the real estate alone when the two values are written separately.

Some deeds owe no tax. The state exemptions include:

  • a transfer for under $100;
  • family transfers down one or two generations, meaning parent to child and grandparent to grandchild;
  • a court-ordered transfer where the order sets no price;
  • a deed in foreclosure of a government-backed loan;
  • a land contract, until title actually passes to the buyer.

The county act is narrower and omits the family exemption, so a deed to a child can dodge the state share and still owe the county share. Cite the exemption on the deed itself, since a deed with neither a price nor an exemption gets returned.

sections.h2: What formatting does a deed need before the office accepts it?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 sets the intake checklist the register applies, and the county reposts it on its real estate information page. The key points:

  • Dark ink signatures, with every signer's name typed or printed underneath and spelled as in the notary's certificate.
  • The notary's name printed beside the notary's signature.
  • Each grantee's mailing address, and the name and business address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • Letter or legal size sheets, at least 10-point type, white paper of 20-pound weight.
  • A clear top margin of 2.5 inches on page one, half an inch elsewhere, and a first line that names the type of recordable event.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits, with an English translation attached to anything in another language.

A deed that clears every point cannot be refused for its content. One that misses a point is sent back, and the closing waits.

sections.h2: Do Sanilac County warranty deeds need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed does. The treasurer must certify the property's tax status first for $5. Land contracts, assignments of them and any deed containing a warranty covenant follow the same path.

The county's schedule lists no such step for a plain quit claim deed. A quit claim hands over whatever the grantor owns with no promise about title, which suits relatives and estate cleanups but leaves a paying buyer exposed, so market-price buyers usually ask for a warranty deed.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey lists $168,300 as the median home value in Sanilac County. Transfer tax on a sale at that price runs about $1,450, a number to subtract when you compare offers.

sections.h2: How do I pay, and where can I look up recorded documents?
sections.html:
The office takes cash, checks, money orders and debit or credit cards, with checks payable to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. Card payers at the counter show photo ID, and an online payment location exists for remote payers.

Searching costs nothing at rod.sanilaccounty.net, where guest users can look through an index that begins in 1801. Page images come as PDFs at $1 a page, with a $5 charge on every order.

The office also runs a free property fraud alert. Enroll a parcel and the owner is told whenever something new is recorded against it, which helps with a farm field or lake cabin that nobody checks for weeks.

sections.h2: What is Sanilac County like for sellers?
sections.html:
Sanilac County fronts Lake Huron in the Thumb, with Huron County above it, Tuscola and Lapeer to the west, and St. Clair below. Organized in 1849, it counted 40,611 residents in 2020 and an estimated 40,083 in 2025.

Its four cities are Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City, while Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville see seasonal visitors. Six state highways cross it, M-19 through M-90, and level, rich soil keeps farming at the center of many parcels.

  • Share of homes occupied by their owners: 82.6 percent.
  • Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $1,226.
  • Median rent: $807.
  • Median household income: $58,863.
  • New building permits in 2025: 74.

Local families and lake-home shoppers make up much of the buyer pool, and an inland farmhouse reaches a different audience than a cottage at the shore.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Sanilac County deed?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, however many pages, under MCL 600.2567. Assignments or discharges that cover several instruments add $3 for each additional one.

faqs.q: What do the state and county transfer taxes add up to here?
faqs.a: Together they come to $8.60 per $1,000 of price, with $7.50 going to the state and $1.10 to the county. The seller owes $1,720 on a $200,000 sale.

faqs.q: Can a deed be mailed to the Sanilac County recorder?
faqs.a: Call (810) 648-2313 first to confirm the total for recording, tax and any certificate. A deed that falls short of MCL 565.201 comes back unrecorded.

faqs.q: Must the treasurer approve my deed before it is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes for a warranty deed or land contract. The treasurer's certificate costs $5, and the certified deed then goes to the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Is a gift of a house to my child taxed on transfer?
faqs.a: The state tax does not apply to a deed from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild. The county tax has no such exemption, so confirm the figure with the office before recording.
